subject: Need help to understand how server and client communicate

messages.author: 43b6c2f7e9e0e9b0
messages.subject: Need help to understand how server and client communicate
parts:
Hello,

My name is Junghoon Lee, and my friend, his students and myself are developing an R library called RIGHT (R Interactive Graphics via HTml) for interactive visualization using JavaScript and HTML5 canvas. Just to give you some idea about what we are doing, here is a demo video the students created some time ago: http://youtube.googleapis.com/v/thlwjYFC_yY?vq=hd1080;hd=1;autoplay=1; If you are interested, we will be happy to discuss more.

We thought that it would be interesting to make our interactive plots become both input and output to Shiny in order to do something like this:

* An interactive plot contains data (imagine a scatter plot) and an overlaid line representing some model fit  
* RIGHT will let users select outliers and hide them
* Shiny refits the model with updated data excluding outliers
* The fitted line is updated

Such a capability can be a nice addition to Shiny since RIGHT can provide rich client side interactivity for visualized data and Shiny can help us perform more interesting computation on the server side.

Can you help us gain some understanding of how Shiny server and client communicate? At the end of the day, RIGHT probably has to send and receive some kind of data frame (array of objects) to and from the Shiny server. We started to look into your code, but any pointers on where to start or a simple example code will be very helpful.

Thank you very much!

Sincerely,
Junghoon Lee

messages.subject: Re: Need help to understand how server and client communicate
parts:
Dear Joe,

Thank you so much for your quick response, and it will be my pleasure to talk to you once you return from UseR conference. 

Meanwhile, I asked one of our students to do the following since he is working on this project as part of Google Summer of Code (the complete proposal is no longer available for some reason). He has to make some pretty rapid progress.
  • Create an example where
    • ui.R uses textInput() (see shiny manual at http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/shiny/shiny.pdf)
    • server.R simply prints the value out using cat() function (debugging techniques at http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#run-and-debug can be useful)
  • Look at the created JavaScript code and try to understand how the text is passed to the server. Try to modify the code so that you can pass an object array in JavaScript, like an array of (x, y) values. You may have to encode the data into a string to do this for now.
  • tableOutput() and renderTable() functions may be some help to learn how to encode the data. See the tutorial at http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#shiny-text. 
The key challenge for now is to learn how to communicate an object array of, say, (x,y) value between the client and the server. For the moment, we will completely generate client-side JavaScript code based on what Shiny does.  We will try to create a wrapper to make RIGHT an input/output to Shiny once the prototype works,

Please let me know if you have any suggestions, and wish you a safe trip.

Sincerely,
Junghoon Lee

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Need help to understand how server and client communicate
parts:
For sending data from client to server, check out Shiny.onInputChange(name, value), where value can be anything that can be translated to JSON.

For sending data from server to client, look at the renderText/renderTable/etc. functions as you suggested; those are for sending things that feel like "the main value of this output"; for sending directives to outputs that are not necessarily their "main" value, you can use session$sendCustomMessage(type, value) in server.R, paired with Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler(type, function(value) { ... }) on the client.

See https://github.com/jcheng5/leaflet-shiny for an extensive example of using both of these techniques.

messages.author: 43b6c2f7e9e0e9b0
messages.subject: Re: Need help to understand how server and client communicate
parts:
Joe,

Please let me add a few things to ChungHa's question. We initially added something like 

exports.onInputChange("TestEntry", {a:[1, 2], b:[3, 4]});

directly to shiny.js, and we found that it works properly. However, when we tried to do this in www/index.html file like the following (to avoid editing shiny.js)

<head>
...
<script src="shared/shiny.js" type="text/javascript"></script>
<script>window.Shiny.onInputChange("TestEntry", {a:[1, 2], b:[3, 4]})</script>
...

nothing gets sent to the server.. This is probably a dumb JavaScript question, but how do we get around this? It seems to us that window.Shiny (or exports) is not visible outside of shiny.js

One additional question we have is related to reformatting data. When we send {a:[1, 2], b:[3, 4]} from JavaScript (client) to R (server), we found that the received input$TestEntry is a list of lists. Is there a way to reformat this behind the scene so that input$TestEntry becomes a data.frame object? We can manually reformat this by something like as.data.frame(lapply(input$TestEntry, unlist)), and we found a similar function for matrices (unpackMatrix) that you wrote, but we are wondering whether we can do this without intervention.

Thank you very much!

Sincerely,
Junghoon Lee

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Need help to understand how server and client communicate
parts:
The script you included in your e-mail doesn't send anything because Shiny has not been initialized yet. Instead you would have to do something like this:

$(function() {
  setTimeout(function() {
    // Your code goes here
  }, 10)
});

This is for values that have to be sent at startup (though I'd love to know why you are sending values at startup, we haven't seen this as necessary so far--usually values are part of inputs, which have their own API as documented in the tutorial).

It is admittedly a little gross that you have to use this setTimeout to know when Shiny has finished initializing, perhaps we can make an event for that in the future.

As for your other question, there is not currently a way to automatically format those values, sorry. I have a TODO in the code to let users add their own unpackMatrix-like functions but it doesn't exist today.
